title: Diagnose Big Billion Days returns spike
persona: Arjun, PM on Flipkart's fashion vertical
scenario: Returns rate on women's ethnic wear jumped from 22% to 41% in the 10 days after Big Billion Days. Top three return reasons in the form: ‘size mismatch’, ‘colour different in real life’, ‘changed my mind’. You have order-level data, return-reason tags, and a sample of 200 returned-item photos from the warehouse. You don't have customer call recordings. Tomorrow you owe category leadership a hypothesis-led memo, not a redesign.
badPrompt: why are returns going up on flipkart fashion?
badOutput: Returns can go up for many reasons, sizing, quality, expectations, post-sale buyer's remorse. You should look at the data and improve product photos, size charts, and reviews to reduce returns.

hints.title: Anchor the data you have
hints.body: Name what you have (return-reason tags, warehouse photos) AND what you don't (no call recordings). Claude will calibrate around the gap.

hints.title: Add a negative
hints.body: Tell Claude NOT to propose redesigns. Diagnosis only, ranked by likelihood, with a confirm/deny check for each hypothesis.

checks.tip: State the diagnostic intent. You want hypotheses, not solutions.
Name the specific metric and category, returns rate on ethnic wear.
Anchor the timing, post-Big Billion Days. Sale-driven returns behave differently.
Include the magnitude, 22%, 41%, in 10 days. Decision-grade context.
Name the data you have AND the data you don't have.
Add a negative constraint, do NOT propose redesigns or solutions.
Ask Claude to rank hypotheses by likelihood, don't treat them as equal.
Reference the leadership audience and the deadline. It shapes the answer.
Use chain-of-thought, walk through reasoning before listing hypotheses.
Specify a structured output, hypothesis + confirm/deny check for each.

tipIfLow: The unlock is the negative constraint plus the data inventory. The strong ask is: ‘Rank these 5 hypotheses by likelihood given that the spike is post-BBD on ethnic wear, and we have return-reason tags + warehouse photos but no call recordings. For each hypothesis, give one confirm and one deny check we could run in 48 hours.’
goldPrompt: You are a senior PM partner at Flipkart. I'm Arjun, fashion-vertical PM. Returns on women's ethnic wear jumped 22%→41% in the 10 days after Big Billion Days 2026. I have order-level data, return-reason tags ('size mismatch', 'colour different', 'changed my mind'), and a sample of 200 warehouse photos. I do NOT have call recordings. Tomorrow I owe category leadership a hypothesis-led memo — diagnosis only, no redesigns. Output: 5 ranked hypotheses by likelihood. For each, give one confirm-check and one deny-check I can run in 48 hours using only the data I named. If a hypothesis needs data I haven't shared, say so explicitly. Walk through your reasoning before listing the table.
